title: Artefact Dependency Maps Storage Design
topic: <research>-r: research Rally dependency handling, critical-path storage, Vector implementation model, and whether Contraction Hierarchies fit.
summary: Rally-style dependency edges should be Vector's source of truth; critical paths are computed projections.

1. Overview

This paper researches how Vector should persist and compute artefact dependencies for the new dependency-map surface. The immediate product requirement is user-authored dependency assignment across three states: Requires First, In Parallel, and Unlocks Next. The deeper requirement is a durable critical-path substrate where many maps can overlap, share artefacts, survive focus changes, and warn when deleting an artefact would break a path.

The research anchor is Rally by Broadcom because Rally has long-standing predecessor/successor dependency behaviour. Rally's public material points toward a simple product lesson: store dependency relationships on artefacts as predecessor/successor links, then build scoped views, widgets, and frame-of-reference maps over those links. Vector should follow that pattern, with stronger Sentinel enforcement and with explicit topology-node ownership.

2. Key Findings

  • Use edge rows as the source of truth. Dependencies should be persisted as UUID-to-UUID artefact edges. Canvas buckets, reverse lookup, impact warnings, and critical-path calculations should be read projections over those edges.
  • Do not store the three UI buckets as JSON on the target artefact. Bucket JSON would make reverse lookup, duplicate prevention, deletion impact checks, and cross-map overlap fragile.
  • Rally validates the frame-of-reference design. Broadcom's Rally article says the Release Dependencies view maps all User Story dependencies and can become tangled, so Rally simplifies the display through a frame-of-reference view where left-to-right position carries dependency meaning [1]. Vector's focused target canvas is the same idea.
  • Rally exposes dependency links as queryable predecessor/successor collections. Broadcom community guidance shows queries against fields such as Predecessors.Project.ObjectID and notes that scope must allow access to related items outside the current project [2]. This maps directly to Vector's need for Sentinel-gated cross-node search.
  • In Parallel is not a CPM dependency. Requires First and Unlocks Next map cleanly to directed finish-to-start edges. In Parallel is an associative relationship and should not participate in DAG cycle rejection or CPM longest-path math unless a future rule deliberately converts it into a schedule constraint.
  • Critical path is a computed projection. CPM uses a forward pass, backward pass, and float calculation after dependencies and durations exist [6]. It should not define the base schema.
  • Contraction Hierarchies are premature for writes. CH is powerful for fast shortest-path routing after preprocessing [9], but our graph is user-edited, relatively small per map, and needs correctness under mutation. Start with edge rows plus optional reachability/cache tables; consider CH only if future graph-query volumes justify it.

3. Rally Findings

Predecessor and successor links

Rally's public help/community material consistently talks about dependencies through Predecessors and Successors fields. A Broadcom Product reply gives example queries against predecessor project fields and recommends Cross Team Dependencies widgets for viewing predecessor/successor relationships in scope [2]. A separate Broadcom KB article gives a dependency-query workaround using Predecessors.FormattedID and Successors.FormattedID, again confirming dependency collections are first-class query fields on artefacts [4].

Frame of reference, not global hairball

The Rally Release Dependencies article is especially relevant to our canvas. It explains that the application maps all dependencies for all User Stories and can become tangled, so it uses a frame-of-reference view. The article tells users to read columns from left to right: an artefact to the left is needed before the middle, and the middle is needed before the right [1]. That supports Vector's target-focused V2 map: do not attempt to show every chain at once; show the active artefact as the frame of reference and derive buckets from its adjacent edges.

Scope matters

Rally guidance warns that dependency queries only work if the app or widget is scoped so it can access items outside the current project [2]. Rally Office Hours also notes that cross-ART dependency lists can show cross-ART dependencies if the user has visibility [5]. Vector must do the same through Sentinel: every candidate search and every edge read/write must be bounded by the caller's tenant, workspace, and allowed topology nodes.

Object model, not direct database

Broadcom's data-dictionary article says Rally does not expose direct database access and points users to an object model instead [3]. The lesson for Vector is not to expose dependency tables as a public contract. The public contract should be typed siteAPI endpoints and DTOs; physical tables remain internal and are free to evolve.

4. Vector Storage Model

Vector already stores artefact hierarchy separately on artefacts.artefacts_id_parent, with artefacts_id_topology_node carrying topology placement. The dependency map must not reuse parentage. Parentage is a tree; dependencies are a graph.

Recommended tables

TablePurposeCore columns
artefact_dependency_mapsUser-visible dependency/critical-path container.artefact_dependency_maps_id, ..._id_subscription, ..._id_workspace, ..._id_topology_node, ..._id_root_artefact, ..._name, created/updated/archived fields.
artefact_dependency_edgesCanonical relationship between two artefacts inside a map.artefact_dependency_edges_id, ..._id_map, ..._id_from_artefact, ..._id_to_artefact, ..._kind, ..._pair_low, ..._pair_high, created/updated/archived fields.
artefact_dependency_edge_eventsAppend-only audit/history for add/remove/broken-by-archive events.event_id, edge/map ids, actor id, event kind, before/after JSON, timestamp.
artefact_dependency_projection (later)Optional computed cache for CPM/reachability.map id, artefact id, earliest/latest fields, float, critical flag, stale marker.

Edge kinds

UI stateStored edgeMeaning when target is focusedDAG check?
Requires Firstfrom = required artefact, to = target, kind = finish_to_startThe related artefact must complete before target can proceed.Yes
Unlocks Nextfrom = target, to = successor artefact, kind = finish_to_startThe target enables the related artefact.Yes
In ParallelCanonical ordered pair, kind = parallelThe related artefact is associated with target but does not gate it.No

This lets reverse lookup fall out naturally. If Story 5 requires Story 3, the single stored edge is 3 -> 5. When Story 5 is focused, Story 3 appears in Requires First. When Story 3 is focused, Story 5 appears in Unlocks Next.

Uniqueness and duplicate prevention

The backend should prevent the same artefact from being allocated twice for the same focused target within the same map. Store canonical pair columns (pair_low, pair_high) and enforce an active-row uniqueness rule across (map_id, pair_low, pair_high). PostgreSQL unique constraints/indexes are the correct primitive for this because they enforce correctness even if the client races or retries [8].

For directed finish_to_start edges, the service should also reject reverse duplicates by cycle detection. A two-node reverse edge would create a cycle. PostgreSQL recursive CTEs support explicit cycle detection via the CYCLE clause, which is suitable for validation queries before insert [7].

Maps and topology ownership

A dependency map should belong to one topology node via artefact_dependency_maps_id_topology_node. That node is the storage and ownership anchor. Edge endpoints may be from the same node or other nodes visible to the user, depending on product rules. If cross-node dependency maps are allowed, the rule is: the map owner node must be in the user's clamp, and every endpoint artefact must also be visible through Sentinel. Names are never authority; all joins use UUIDs.

5. API and Sentinel

All dependency APIs should live behind siteAPI and Sentinel. No dependency endpoint should accept null/no-Sentinel paths. The ?meg= value remains a narrow focus hint, never authority.

Proposed endpoints

EndpointPurposeNotes
GET /dependencies/maps?ash=<artefact_uuid>&meg=<node_uuid>Load maps involving the focused artefact.Returns map headers and current target-relative buckets.
POST /dependencies/mapsCreate a dependency map anchored to a topology node/root artefact.Requires Sentinel clamp on map node and root artefact.
GET /dependencies/maps/{id}Load full map graph.Returns all edge rows visible to caller.
POST /dependencies/maps/{id}/edgesAdd Requires/Unlocks/Parallel relationship.Transactionally validates pair uniqueness, endpoint visibility, and directed-cycle safety.
DELETE /dependencies/maps/{id}/edges/{edge_id}Remove a relationship.Soft-archive edge and append event.
POST /dependencies/maps/{id}/candidates/querySearch candidate artefacts for a focused target.Uses same type/node filters as current UI, excludes already-linked candidates.
GET /work-items/{id}/dependency-impactPreflight archive/delete impact.Used by delete confirmation to list maps/edges that would break.

Sentinel checks

  • Map header read/write: map subscription, workspace, and topology node must match the caller's Sentinel clamp.
  • Candidate search: every candidate comes from work-item query paths already clamped by topology.
  • Edge insert: both endpoint artefacts are loaded by UUID and checked against the caller's clamp before write.
  • Archive/delete impact: impact rows are only returned for maps and artefacts the caller can see; cross-tenant existence must remain invisible.
  • Mutation audit: every edge create/delete/broken event records actor, subscription, workspace, map, edge, and source transport.

6. UI Behaviour

Candidate exclusion

When an artefact is allocated to any state for the current target/map, remove it immediately from the searchable candidate list. Do this optimistically in React for feel, but also make the backend candidate query exclude already-linked candidates. The backend is the authority.

State derivation

Focused targetBucket query
Requires FirstActive finish_to_start edges where to_artefact_id = target_id.
Unlocks NextActive finish_to_start edges where from_artefact_id = target_id.
In ParallelActive parallel edges where either endpoint equals target.

The UI should never store its own permanent bucket arrays. It should render buckets from edge rows, which also solves focus switching and reverse lookup.

Deletion warning

The existing artefact archive path is a direct soft-archive. Before archiving, the backend should query active dependency edges containing that artefact. If any exist, return 409 dependency_impact with the impacted maps and edge count. The confirmation popup should list the impacted paths and either block or require an explicit destructive confirmation. By default, block is safer. If forced archive is later allowed, edge rows should be marked broken/archived and event rows should record the break.

7. Critical Path Computation

Critical path should be computed after the graph exists. CPM is based on task/artefact duration, dependency ordering, and forward/backward passes to calculate earliest start/finish, latest start/finish, and float [6].

Phase 1 computation

  • Only include directed finish_to_start edges.
  • Ignore parallel edges for CPM math; show them visually only.
  • Use topological sort over the directed edge set.
  • Reject cycles before calculation.
  • Use a duration source agreed by product: plan estimate, story points converted by team velocity, or explicit duration field. Do not infer duration from title/type.
  • Compute ES/EF with forward pass, LS/LF with backward pass, then float.
  • Mark artefacts critical where float is zero or under a configurable threshold.

Phase 2 computation

  • Add support for SS/FF/SF and lag only if users need schedule-grade modelling.
  • Add multiple-map rollups: a shared artefact can be critical in one map and non-critical in another.
  • Add projection cache for large maps or dashboards. Keep it rebuildable from edge rows.

8. Contraction Hierarchies

Contraction Hierarchies are a graph-routing acceleration technique. The cited paper describes preprocessing a road network by adding shortcut edges, then answering exact shortest-path queries very quickly with modified bidirectional Dijkstra [9]. That is impressive, but it is optimized for many shortest-path queries over a mostly stable graph.

Vector's dependency graph is different. It is user-edited, scoped by Sentinel, and the immediate query is not global shortest path. It is target-relative bucket lookup, reverse lookup, cycle detection, deletion impact, and eventually longest-path/float calculation. Those are better served initially by indexes, recursive CTEs, and optionally a materialized reachability/projection table.

Recommendation: do not implement Contraction Hierarchies in the first dependency-map release. Revisit only if we later have very large cross-node graphs and repeated route queries such as shortest path between any two artefacts, what-if route exploration, or dependency heatmaps across thousands of artefacts.

9. Implementation Sequence

  1. Migration 1: add artefact_dependency_maps, artefact_dependency_edges, and artefact_dependency_edge_events.
  2. Backend service: create backend/internal/dependencies as the sole writer for maps and edges.
  3. Sentinel integration: all reads/writes require authenticated user, subscription/workspace, map topology node clamp, and endpoint artefact visibility.
  4. Candidate endpoint: wrap existing work-item query logic but exclude already-linked artefacts for the focused target/map.
  5. UI persistence: replace local bucket state with API-loaded buckets; keep optimistic UI but reconcile from backend response.
  6. Archive guard: add dependency-impact preflight before ArchiveWorkItem and surface the result in the delete confirmation flow.
  7. CPM projection: add calculation service once the storage/read/write behaviour is stable.
  8. Performance projection: add reachability/cache tables only when map size or dashboard queries prove they are needed.

10. Gaps

  • Broadcom's detailed Rally TechDocs pages for Cross Team Dependencies were not directly accessible through search in this session. The strongest Rally evidence came from Broadcom KB/community/academy pages.
  • Rally's physical database schema is not public; Broadcom explicitly points users at an object model/API instead of a data dictionary [3]. Schema comparisons are therefore behavioural, not table-for-table.
  • The exact Vector duration source for CPM is unresolved. We need a product decision before calculating schedule dates.
  • The product rule for cross-node dependency maps needs confirmation: allow any Sentinel-visible node, or restrict endpoints to the owning map node/subtree?
  • Delete behaviour needs a product choice: hard block until links are removed, or allow explicit forced archive that marks dependency edges broken.
